editor_note: None of the 8 rewritten entries changes the meaning. For example, entry 13's "menguraikan Gate yang membelitkan (entangling) Qubit yang tidak berdekatan" keeps the English sense. There are a few term splits a native editor would still fix. The rewritten entries 15 and 19 use "mitigasi error", but the rest of the page uses "mitigasi kesalahan" (entries 9, 26, 29, 30), and entry 15 uses "tools" where entry 4 says "alat". Entry 19 translates the PNA title as "Penyerapan noise yang dipropagasikan", but entry 30 refers back to the same technique in English as "propagated noise absorption (PNA)", so the cross-reference is harder to follow. Entry 19 also renders "custom" as "khusus" (special/specific) instead of "kustom", and entry 27 leans on English ("di-sampling", "hardware-efficient", "kode spacetime").

examples.source: Build custom error mitigation pipelines with techniques such as PEC, ZNE, and TREX
examples.translation: Bangun pipeline mitigasi error khusus dengan teknik seperti PEC, ZNE, dan TREX
examples.suggested: Bangun pipeline mitigasi kesalahan kustom dengan teknik seperti PEC, ZNE, dan TREX
examples.why: The page's established rendering is "mitigasi kesalahan" (entries 9, 26, 29, 30). "khusus" reads as "special/specific", while "kustom" matches the English "custom".

examples.source: Propagated noise absorption
examples.translation: Penyerapan noise yang dipropagasikan
examples.suggested: Propagated noise absorption (penyerapan noise terpropagasi)
examples.why: Entry 30 refers to this technique in English as "propagated noise absorption (PNA)". Translating only the card title breaks the link between the two, even though the similar title "Shaded lightcones" stays in English.

examples.source: Use the following tools for learning and refining noise models as part of your error mitigation strategy
examples.translation: Gunakan tools berikut untuk mempelajari dan menyempurnakan model noise sebagai bagian dari strategi mitigasi error kamu
examples.suggested: Gunakan alat berikut untuk mempelajari dan menyempurnakan model noise sebagai bagian dari strategi mitigasi kesalahan kamu
examples.why: Entry 4 renders "tools" as "alat" and the page otherwise uses "kesalahan" for "error". The rewrite brings in English words the rest of the page does not use.

examples.source: Boost the fidelity of sampled distributions using hardware-efficient Pauli checks based on spacetime codes.
examples.translation: Tingkatkan fidelitas distribusi yang di-sampling dengan pemeriksaan Pauli yang hardware-efficient berdasarkan kode spacetime.
examples.suggested: Tingkatkan fidelitas distribusi hasil sampling dengan pemeriksaan Pauli yang efisien untuk perangkat keras, berdasarkan kode ruang-waktu.
examples.why: The hybrid "di-sampling" and the untranslated "hardware-efficient" and "spacetime" read like code-switching. Entry 25 already uses "hasil sampling", and "ruang-waktu" is the standard Indonesian term.

editor_note: All four rewritten entries (4, 6, 14, 20) are faithful, with nothing a learner could misread. Entry 14 keeps the LSB/MSB convention as "bit paling tidak signifikan"/"paling signifikan" and keeps the bit 0 = `0`, bit 1 = `1` → `2` example intact. Entry 20 correctly renders "amplitudo pada indeks $x$ merepresentasikan keadaan basis komputasi $|x\rangle$", and entry 6 uses the informal "kamu" register.

Both rewritten headings translate an IBM product name that the rest of the page keeps in English. Entry 5 renders "IBM Quantum Compute Service" as "Layanan Komputasi IBM Quantum", but entries 0, 6 and 12 keep "IBM Quantum Compute Service". Entry 13 renders "IBM Quantum Platform" as "Platform IBM Quantum", but entries 0, 14, 15, 16, 18 and 28 keep "IBM Quantum Platform". The meaning is unchanged and a learner will still recognise each service, but the section headings now don't match the product names used in the text under them, so both headings should revert to the English names.

examples.source: IBM Quantum Compute Service {#ibm-quantum-compute-service}
examples.translation: Layanan Komputasi IBM Quantum {#ibm-quantum-compute-service}
examples.suggested: IBM Quantum Compute Service {#ibm-quantum-compute-service}
examples.why: This is a proper product name, and the page keeps it in English everywhere else (entries 0, 6, 12). Translating only the heading is inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: IBM Quantum Platform {#ibm-quantum-platform}
examples.translation: Platform IBM Quantum {#ibm-quantum-platform}
examples.suggested: IBM Quantum Platform {#ibm-quantum-platform}
examples.why: This is a proper product name, and the text right under the heading (entries 14 to 16) and entries 0, 18 and 28 keep it as 'IBM Quantum Platform'. Reordering it only in the heading is inconsistent.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries (13, 20, 22, 27) would mislead a learner. Postselection, extrapolation, template circuit/samplex and the Executor workflow all match the English. There are small editorial slips. Entry 22 renders "bound circuits" two ways in the same paragraph ("Circuit yang telah di-bind" and the English-ordered "Circuit bound"), and its parenthetical "selain memiliki nilai parameter yang berbeda yang ditetapkan padanya" is a stiff calque. Entry 20 turns the normative "should be treated as" into the plainer "dianggap". Entry 27 writes "apapun" where standard spelling is "apa pun".

examples.source: what bound circuits to run
examples.translation: Circuit bound mana yang harus dijalankan
examples.suggested: Circuit yang telah di-bind mana yang harus dijalankan
examples.why: The same paragraph and entry 27 use 'Circuit yang telah di-bind'. 'Circuit bound' keeps the English adjective order and is inconsistent with that.

examples.source: (other than having different parameter values assigned to it)
examples.translation: (selain memiliki nilai parameter yang berbeda yang ditetapkan padanya)
examples.suggested: (selain diberi nilai parameter yang berbeda)
examples.why: The double 'yang' and 'ditetapkan padanya' are a calque of the English. A native writer would use the passive 'diberi'.

examples.source: collections of circuit operations that should be treated as having a stable noise context
examples.translation: kumpulan operasi Circuit yang dianggap memiliki konteks noise yang stabil
examples.suggested: kumpulan operasi Circuit yang perlu diperlakukan sebagai memiliki konteks noise yang stabil
examples.why: 'dianggap' drops the normative 'should be treated as', which is the user's modelling choice. The loss is slight and does not mislead.

examples.source: does not make any implicit decisions for you
examples.translation: tidak membuat keputusan implisit apapun untukmu
examples.suggested: tidak membuat keputusan implisit apa pun untukmu
examples.why: Standard Indonesian (KBBI/EYD) writes 'apa pun' as two words.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries (12 and 13) keep the meaning, and nothing in them would mislead a learner. Entry 12 translates "learning offerings" word for word as "penawaran pembelajaran", which sounds like a sales pitch in Indonesian; "materi pembelajaran" reads more naturally. Entry 13's "memfasilitasi pembangunan pengetahuan dan keterampilan" is a stiff noun-heavy calque that a native writer would put as "membantu membangun pengetahuan dan keterampilan". The phrase "rangkaian pembelajaran, dokumentasi, dan konten tutorial yang dikurasi" would also read better as "rangkaian konten pembelajaran, dokumentasi, dan tutorial pilihan".

examples.source: Explore our free learning offerings, such as full courses and classroom modules.
examples.translation: Jelajahi penawaran pembelajaran gratis kami, seperti kursus lengkap dan modul kelas.
examples.suggested: Jelajahi materi pembelajaran gratis kami, seperti kursus lengkap dan modul kelas.
examples.why: 'penawaran' copies 'offerings' word for word and reads like a commercial offer; 'materi pembelajaran' is the natural phrase.

examples.source: Explore curated sequences of learning, documentation, and tutorial content designed to facilitate knowledge and skill-building in specific interest areas.
examples.translation: Jelajahi rangkaian pembelajaran, dokumentasi, dan konten tutorial yang dikurasi, yang dirancang untuk memfasilitasi pembangunan pengetahuan dan keterampilan di area minat tertentu.
examples.suggested: Jelajahi rangkaian konten pembelajaran, dokumentasi, dan tutorial pilihan yang dirancang untuk membantu membangun pengetahuan dan keterampilan di bidang minat tertentu.
examples.why: 'memfasilitasi pembangunan' is a stiff nominalized calque, and the double 'yang ..., yang ...' clause is clunky. 'membantu membangun' and 'bidang minat' read more naturally.

editor_note: Entry 9 is faithful and reads naturally: "Cek secara berkala … untuk melihat rilis baru" and "sering memperbarui persyaratan versi `qiskit-ibm-runtime`" keep the recommendation's strength and the -U upgrade meaning, and nothing was added or dropped.

The five rewritten entries all keep their meaning, including the caveat in the note at [32] that local Rust changes are "tidak akan tercermin ... kecuali kamu membangun ulang ekstensi" by rerunning `build_rust`; "compiler Rust" and "Instal ... dari sumber" also match the rest of the page.

Both rewritten entries match the English: [25] keeps the "limited" condition and the queued-vs-running contrast ("workload yang tertunda akan tetap berada di antrean ... namun, workload yang sedang aktif akan terus berjalan, termasuk workload dalam mode session"), and [26] correctly says "tidak dibatasi" leads to "prioritas lebih rendah" and "waktu antrean yang lebih lama", using the same terms as entry [20].

Entries 0, 4 and 5 are accurate and read naturally. "Scales with the number of shots" becomes "meningkat seiring dengan jumlah shots", and entry 4 keeps the point that lower Estimator precision needs more shots. Entry 7 has one small softening. The English says a noise model "becomes stale after a certain time", but the Indonesian says it "bisa menjadi kedaluwarsa", which means it only might go stale. The advice that follows still holds, so a learner would not be misled, but the sentence should state it as a fact, as the English does.

examples.source: Note that a noise model becomes stale after a certain time
examples.translation: Perlu diingat bahwa noise model bisa menjadi kedaluwarsa setelah jangka waktu tertentu
examples.suggested: Perlu diingat bahwa noise model akan kedaluwarsa setelah jangka waktu tertentu
examples.why: Adding 'bisa' ('can/may') makes a definite claim sound only possible. The conclusion that reuse only works without long delays is kept, so this is minor, but the Indonesian caveat is weaker than the English.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning and would not mislead a learner, but a native editor would still change three things. In entry 27 the link text is "Primitif IBM Quantum", yet the same sentence says "primitive dasar" and entry 37 links to the same page as "IBM Quantum primitives", so one concept gets two spellings side by side. In entry 34, "Juga," at the start of a sentence is a calque of English "Also,"; "Selain itu," is the natural opener. Also in entry 34, "mengaktifkan opsi" (turn on options) is a poor fit for adjusting a level setting like resilience_level; "mengatur" fits better.

examples.source: The [IBM Quantum primitives](/guides/qiskit-runtime-primitives), ...
examples.translation: [Primitif IBM Quantum](/guides/qiskit-runtime-primitives), ... Implementasi primitive dasar ini ...
examples.suggested: [IBM Quantum primitives](/guides/qiskit-runtime-primitives), ... Implementasi primitive dasar ini ...
examples.why: The Indonesian spelling 'Primitif' sits in the same sentence as 'primitive', while the rest of the file keeps 'primitives'/'primitive', including entry 37's link to the same page.

examples.source: Also, because of the additional layer of abstraction, you might be able to more easily access ...
examples.translation: Juga, karena adanya lapisan abstraksi tambahan, kamu mungkin bisa lebih mudah mengakses ...
examples.suggested: Selain itu, karena adanya lapisan abstraksi tambahan, kamu mungkin bisa lebih mudah mengakses ...
examples.why: Starting a sentence with 'Juga,' copies English word order. Native technical writing uses 'Selain itu,'.

examples.source: by toggling options such as the primitive's resilience_level
examples.translation: dengan mengaktifkan opsi seperti resilience_level pada primitive
examples.suggested: dengan mengatur opsi seperti resilience_level pada primitive
examples.why: resilience_level is set to a level, not switched on or off, so 'mengaktifkan' (turn on) is slightly off. 'mengatur' (set/adjust) is closer to 'toggling'.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning. In entry 3, the deprecation dates and versions (early 2025, v1.3.0 to v2.0.0) are correct, 'deprecated' is rendered as 'tidak digunakan lagi' (the usual Indonesian wording), and 'might lead to' is correctly softened to 'berpotensi membawa'. Entry 5 has two small wording problems. 'mengkalibrasi' is not the standard KBBI form, which is 'mengalibrasi' because the k drops. 'pada sudut tertentu' ('at a certain angle') loses the idea that the user chooses the angle ('a specified angle'), so 'pada sudut yang ditentukan' is closer.

examples.source: to calibrate the single- and two-qubit rotations
examples.translation: untuk mengkalibrasi rotasi qubit tunggal dan dua qubit
examples.suggested: untuk mengalibrasi rotasi qubit tunggal dan dua qubit
examples.why: KBBI standard form drops the initial k after meng- (kalibrasi -> mengalibrasi).

examples.source: for a specified angle
examples.translation: pada sudut tertentu
examples.suggested: untuk sudut yang ditentukan
examples.why: 'tertentu' reads as 'some particular angle'; the English means an angle the user specifies. The nuance is slight and not misleading.

editor_note: All five rewritten entries (76, 100, 104, 111, 159) keep their meaning, and none of them misleads. Entry 76 correctly says that V1 required the number of circuits to match the number of observables and parameter sets ("jumlah circuit input harus cocok dengan jumlah observable dan set parameter"), entry 104 keeps the "tidak lagi diizinkan" negation, and entry 159 keeps the cause "Qiskit Aer menghapus fungsionalitas simulasi" and uses the correct kamu register.

Entry 6 is faithful in meaning and will not mislead a learner. It keeps the "typically" hedge as "biasanya", the purpose of the reset (qubits initialized to zero) and the `init_qubits` flag as a primitive execution option. The one problem is terminology: the same sentence calls the circuit both "sebuah sirkuit" and "di awal Circuit", while the rest of the page (entries 7, 8, 10, 12, 13) uses lowercase "circuit" throughout. Use "circuit" in both places to match the rest of the page.

examples.source: When a circuit is executed on an IBM® quantum processing unit (QPU), an implicit reset is typically inserted at the beginning of the circuit
examples.translation: Saat sebuah sirkuit dieksekusi pada unit pemrosesan kuantum (QPU) IBM®, biasanya dilakukan reset implisit di awal Circuit
examples.suggested: Saat sebuah circuit dieksekusi pada unit pemrosesan kuantum (QPU) IBM®, biasanya dilakukan reset implisit di awal circuit
examples.why: 'circuit' is written two different ways in one sentence ('sirkuit' / 'Circuit'), and neither matches the lowercase 'circuit' the rest of the page uses.

editor_note: Neither rewritten entry changes the meaning. Entries 6 and 30 still say the same things as the English about PUBs, run(), the job lifecycle and the ExecutionSpan start/stop timing bounds. The problems are wording. In entry 6, "workload vektorisasi" uses a noun where an adjective belongs and should be "workload tervektorisasi" (entry 12 keeps "vectorized" in English, so the term is also inconsistent across the file). "Ini digunakan" is a vague stand-in for the plural "They" (the PUBs), and "opsi runtime yang ditentukan dari primitif" copies the English sentence structure too closely. Entry 30 uses "shots", while entry 16 uses the Indonesian-style "shot".

examples.line_approx: Sampler memungkinkan kamu mendefinisikan workload vektorisasi
examples.source: efficiently define vectorized workloads
examples.translation: mendefinisikan workload vektorisasi secara efisien
examples.suggested: mendefinisikan workload tervektorisasi secara efisien
examples.why: 'vektorisasi' is a noun ('vectorization'), so it doesn't work as a modifier here. The adjective form 'tervektorisasi' is correct, and entry 12 leaves 'vectorized' in English, so the term is inconsistent.

examples.line_approx: Ini digunakan sebagai input ... opsi runtime yang ditentukan dari primitif tersebut
examples.source: They are used as inputs ... runtime options specified from the primitive
examples.translation: Ini digunakan sebagai input ... opsi runtime yang ditentukan dari primitif tersebut
examples.suggested: PUB ini digunakan sebagai input ... opsi runtime yang ditetapkan pada primitif tersebut
examples.why: 'Ini' doesn't clearly point back to the PUBs, and 'ditentukan dari' copies the English 'specified from'. 'ditetapkan pada' reads more naturally.

examples.line_approx: waktu eksekusi shots tertentu pada QPU. Shots dikelompokkan
examples.source: when particular shots were executed ... Shots are grouped
examples.translation: waktu eksekusi shots tertentu ... Shots dikelompokkan
examples.suggested: waktu eksekusi shot tertentu ... Shot dikelompokkan
examples.why: Entry 16 uses the singular-style 'shot' ('data shot', 'shot yang terurut'), which follows the Indonesian convention of not marking plurals. The English plural 'shots' is inconsistent within the file.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 5 renders "encrypted at rest" as "dienkripsi saat disimpan (at rest)". Entry 10 keeps both the "(yang belum dihapus)" qualifier and the three-year limit that applies only while you use the service. Entry 7 has one markup slip: the comma that belongs after the link is inside the link text, "[halaman Instances,](…)", so it becomes part of the hyperlink. It should come after the closing parenthesis.

examples.source: from the [Instances page](https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/instances), find the instance
examples.translation: dari [halaman Instances,](https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/instances) temukan instance
examples.suggested: dari [halaman Instances](https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/instances), temukan instance
examples.why: The comma has slipped inside the link text, so the rendered hyperlink reads 'halaman Instances,'. It is cosmetic and does not change the meaning.

editor_note: Entry 6 is faithful: the caveat that reference primitives cannot model noise and that Aer primitives can is kept intact, and the kamu register holds. It does render "quantum circuit(s)" two ways in the same paragraph, "rangkaian kuantum" and then "simulator circuit kuantum", while the rest of the file uses "circuit" throughout. "suffer from errors" also became "rentan terhadap kesalahan" ("prone to errors"), which slightly softens a statement of fact into a tendency. Neither would mislead a learner.

examples.source: to perform exact simulation of quantum circuits
examples.translation: untuk melakukan simulasi eksak dari rangkaian kuantum
examples.suggested: untuk melakukan simulasi eksak circuit kuantum
examples.why: The same entry later says 'simulator circuit kuantum' and the rest of the file uses 'circuit' throughout. Pick one rendering.

examples.source: Currently existing quantum processors suffer from errors, or noise
examples.translation: Prosesor kuantum yang ada saat ini rentan terhadap kesalahan, atau noise
examples.suggested: Prosesor kuantum yang ada saat ini mengalami kesalahan, atau noise
examples.why: 'rentan terhadap' means 'prone to', a slight softening of the English, which says the errors are present now. The meaning is still recognizable.

editor_note: The rewritten heading in entry 22 gets the meaning right, but it turns the product name "IBM Quantum System API" into "API Sistem IBM Quantum". The rest of the page keeps the name in English: entry 24 has "Backend Quantum System API", entry 26 has "Endpoint Quantum System API", and the sibling heading in entry 37 stays "IBM Quantum Compute Service". The heading therefore doesn't match the body text that refers back to it. A reader won't be misled, but a native editor would keep the product name as written, so the heading should read "IBM Quantum System API".

examples.source: IBM Quantum System API {#ibm-quantum-system-api}
examples.translation: API Sistem IBM Quantum {#ibm-quantum-system-api}
examples.suggested: IBM Quantum System API {#ibm-quantum-system-api}
examples.why: This is a product name. Entries 24 and 26 keep it as 'Quantum System API', and the parallel heading in entry 37 keeps 'IBM Quantum Compute Service' in English. Translating only this heading makes it inconsistent with the rest of the page.

editor_note: The three rewritten entries (29, 43, 48) keep the English meaning, and none of them would mislead a learner. The Layout/Routing split, the three-CNOT cost of SWAP and the optimization-stage caveats all come through intact. The problems are small ones. "Noisy" is "berisik" in entries 29 and 48 but "bising" in entry 43, so the rewritten entries disagree with each other. Entry 48 adds an unneeded English gloss, "rutin (routine)", and ends stiffly with "Tahap inilah tempat berbagai optimization level mulai berbeda". Entry 29 also calques "represents" as "mewakili operasi".

examples.source: an expensive operation to perform on noisy quantum devices
examples.translation: operasi yang mahal untuk dijalankan pada perangkat kuantum yang bising
examples.suggested: operasi yang mahal untuk dijalankan pada perangkat kuantum yang berisik (use the same word as entries 29 and 48)
examples.why: 'Noisy' is 'bising' here but 'berisik' in entries 29 and 48. Pick one word for 'noisy' across the rewritten entries.

examples.source: there are many routines for optimizing circuits ... This stage is where the various optimization levels begin to differ.
examples.translation: tersedia banyak rutin (routine) untuk mengoptimalkan Circuit ... Tahap inilah tempat berbagai optimization level mulai berbeda.
examples.suggested: tersedia banyak rutin untuk mengoptimalkan Circuit ... Pada tahap inilah berbagai optimization level mulai berbeda.
examples.why: The English gloss '(routine)' is unnecessary, and 'Tahap inilah tempat ...' reads stiffly. 'Pada tahap inilah ...' is the natural phrasing.

examples.source: Each SWAP gate represents an expensive and noisy operation to perform.
examples.translation: Setiap Gate SWAP mewakili operasi yang mahal dan berisik untuk dilakukan.
examples.suggested: Setiap Gate SWAP merupakan operasi yang mahal dan berisik.
examples.why: 'Mewakili' is a literal calque of 'represents'. 'Merupakan' is what an Indonesian technical writer would use, and the trailing 'untuk dilakukan' is unnecessary.

editor_note: Rewritten entries 2-4 are faithful and read naturally: "hanya mampu menoleransi tingkat kesalahan yang sangat rendah", "mulai berkenalan dengan" for "take a first look", and "*pasangan-pasangan* tertentu dari kode koreksi kesalahan klasik" all keep the English meaning and emphasis.

Entries 8 and 10 are faithful and read naturally. "membutuhkan tersedianya satu qubit ruang kerja" correctly renders the workspace-qubit requirement, and the reuse-or-discard caveat is kept. Entry 23 has the right meaning, but "we can reasonably expect" became "kita bisa mengharapkan". That drops "reasonably", and "mengharapkan" leans toward "hope for" rather than "anticipate", so "cukup beralasan untuk memperkirakan" would be better. The first sentence is also slightly redundant ("operasi itu kemungkinan merupakan operasi yang lebih mahal biayanya"), but nothing here would mislead a learner.

examples.source: we can reasonably expect that the resulting quantum circuit will be larger and more complicated than one for $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}$.
examples.translation: kita bisa mengharapkan bahwa Circuit kuantum yang dihasilkan akan lebih besar dan lebih rumit daripada Circuit kuantum untuk $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}.$
examples.suggested: cukup beralasan bagi kita untuk memperkirakan bahwa Circuit kuantum yang dihasilkan akan lebih besar dan lebih rumit daripada Circuit kuantum untuk $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}.$
examples.why: The 'reasonably' qualifier is dropped, and 'mengharapkan' tends to mean 'hope for'. 'memperkirakan' is the natural word for an expectation you can justify.

editor_note: Entry 17 (the Credly privacy notice) is faithful. It keeps every caveat, including the data shared (nama, alamat email, dan badge yang diperoleh), the fact that sharing is global, and both privacy links. Entry 12 does not mislead, but it has two small problems. It adds "seluruh" ("all of the lessons"), which is not in "after reading the lessons" and slightly strengthens the advice. Its first clause also uses "untuk" twice ("Untuk mendapatkan badge kamu untuk Fundamentals..."), which reads clunky.

examples.source: This exam is intended to be taken after reading the lessons in this course.
examples.translation: Ujian ini sebaiknya dikerjakan setelah kamu membaca seluruh pelajaran dalam kursus ini.
examples.suggested: Ujian ini sebaiknya dikerjakan setelah kamu membaca pelajaran-pelajaran dalam kursus ini.
examples.why: 'seluruh' (all) is added and slightly strengthens the advice beyond the source. The effect is small, but it is not in the English.

examples.source: To earn your badge for Fundamentals of quantum algorithms, take the exam at IBM® Training.
examples.translation: Untuk mendapatkan badge kamu untuk Fundamentals of quantum algorithms, ikuti ujian di IBM® Training.
examples.suggested: Untuk mendapatkan badge Fundamentals of quantum algorithms, ikuti ujian di IBM® Training.
examples.why: Using 'untuk' twice in one clause is a calque of 'To earn ... for ...'. A native editor would drop the second 'untuk' and the redundant 'kamu'.

editor_note: Entries 4 and 5 are faithful and would not mislead a learner. The scope claims survive intact: number theory as a "narrow" domain, and scaling with instance size rather than wall-clock time. Entry 5 renders "hardware" two ways within a few lines, first as "perangkat keras" and then as "hardware", so it should pick one. Entry 4 ends with the calque "(dan mereka juga kebetulan sangat relevan dengan pelajaran yang mengikuti ini)", which uses "mereka" for inanimate problems and should read "pelajaran berikutnya". Entry 5 also calques "in recognition of the fact" as "dengan mengakui fakta bahwa".

examples.source: the ever-improving hardware ... using faster and more reliable hardware
examples.translation: perangkat keras yang terus berkembang ... menggunakan hardware yang lebih cepat
examples.suggested: ... menggunakan perangkat keras yang lebih cepat dan lebih andal
examples.why: The same term is rendered two ways within one paragraph. Use 'perangkat keras' both times.

examples.source: (and they also happen to be highly relevant to the lesson following this one)
examples.translation: (dan mereka juga kebetulan sangat relevan dengan pelajaran yang mengikuti ini)
examples.suggested: (dan kebetulan juga sangat relevan dengan pelajaran berikutnya)
examples.why: 'mereka' for inanimate problems and 'pelajaran yang mengikuti ini' are English calques. A native writer would drop the pronoun and write 'pelajaran berikutnya'.

examples.source: We focus on this aspect of computational cost in recognition of the fact that algorithms have fundamental importance
examples.translation: Kita fokus pada aspek biaya komputasi ini dengan mengakui fakta bahwa algoritma memiliki arti penting yang fundamental
examples.suggested: Kita berfokus pada aspek biaya komputasi ini karena algoritma memiliki peran yang fundamental
examples.why: 'dengan mengakui fakta bahwa' is a stiff literal rendering of 'in recognition of the fact'. A simple 'karena' carries the same meaning naturally.

editor_note: Entries 3–5 keep the meaning faithfully. The definition of purification, the caveat "asalkan bagian sistem gabungan yang di-trace out cukup besar", the dilation idea and the teorema Uhlmann link are all intact, and the terms purifikasi, matriks densitas, keadaan murni and fidelitas are used consistently. Two small edits are left in entry 4. "memikirkannya sebagai merepresentasikan bagian dari..." is a stiff calque of "thinking about them as representing". "Sudah umum dan sangat berguna" adds an intensifier ("sangat", meaning "very") that the English "both common and useful" does not have.

examples.source: by thinking about them as representing parts of larger systems whose states are pure
examples.translation: dengan memikirkannya sebagai merepresentasikan bagian dari sistem yang lebih besar yang keadaannya murni
examples.suggested: dengan memandangnya sebagai representasi bagian dari sistem yang lebih besar yang keadaannya murni
examples.why: 'memikirkannya sebagai merepresentasikan' copies the English gerund structure. A native technical writer would use a noun phrase ('sebagai representasi') or 'memandangnya sebagai'.

examples.source: It's both common and useful to consider purifications of states
examples.translation: Sudah umum dan sangat berguna untuk meninjau purifikasi suatu keadaan
examples.suggested: Meninjau purifikasi suatu keadaan saat menalarnya merupakan hal yang umum sekaligus berguna.
examples.why: 'sangat' (very) slightly strengthens the claim, and 'Sudah umum ... untuk' reads a little like a calque. This does not mislead, so it is minor.

editor_note: Entry 11 is faithful and natural, keeping every element of the privacy notice: Credly as "pemroses data pihak ketiga yang diotorisasi oleh IBM", the "(nama, alamat email, dan lencana yang diperoleh)" data list, the "IBM dapat membagikan" permission, and the informal "kamu"/"-mu" register.

All five rewritten entries are faithful: in [40], "Every other orbital" is correctly rendered as "Setiap orbital kedua (selang-seling)" with the 0th/2nd/4th example intact, and [84] and [92] keep the Q0 flip and "pemulihan konfigurasi self-consistent" consistent with [15]/[20].

None of the three rewritten entries (23, 29, 37) would mislead a learner. Entry 23 keeps the caveat that superposition never shows both results in one measurement, and entry 29 keeps both comparisons (independent randomness, and classical correlation or shared randomness). Two small fixes remain. Entry 37 renders "counts" as "cacahan (counts)", but the rest of the page uses "hitungan" (entry 50) or "jumlah" (entries 41 and 44). Entry 29 spells "memberitahu" as one word, where standard Indonesian (KBBI) spelling is "memberi tahu".

examples.source: and extracting the counts from the results
examples.translation: dan mengekstrak cacahan (counts) dari hasilnya
examples.suggested: dan mengekstrak hitungan (counts) dari hasilnya
examples.why: 'Cacahan' is a defensible word, but the rest of the file uses 'hitungan' or 'jumlah' for counts (entries 41, 44, 50). Using 'hitungan' here makes the page consistent.

examples.line_approx: Mengukur satu qubit memberitahu kamu sesuatu tentang yang lain.
examples.source: Measuring one qubit tells you something about the other.
examples.translation: Mengukur satu qubit memberitahu kamu sesuatu tentang yang lain.
examples.suggested: Mengukur satu qubit memberi tahu kamu sesuatu tentang qubit yang lain.
examples.why: Standard (KBBI) spelling is 'memberi tahu', written as two words. Repeating 'qubit' also reads more naturally than the bare 'yang lain'.
